title: Overloading is resolved at compile time
answer: No. Java overload resolution is performed at compile time using the method name, available overloads, declared argument types, and allowed conversions. Runtime dispatch can subsequently choose an overriding implementation of the already selected instance-method signature, but runtime object type does not cause Java to redo overload selection. This distinction is why an Object-typed variable can select an Object overload even when it refers to a more specific runtime object.
